- Model consistently underestimates true prices, especially in the first 10–15 days of the forecast horizon.
- Forecasts show a gradual upward trend, but true outcomes often spike higher early (e.g., 78–80) and then decline, suggesting model fails to capture short-term volatility or policy-driven surges.
- Model overreacts to recent price drops, producing a “sudden dip” followed by a slow recovery — overshoots after sharp declines.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: forecasts trend upward but fail to account for sharp downward corrections in the middle of the horizon.
- Forecasts lag behind true price movements by 2–5 days, particularly in the first 10 days — model is slow to react to new data.
- Model overestimates the “bottom” of a price drop and underestimates the “top” of a price rise — especially after spikes.
- Model fails to adjust for seasonal or policy-driven price shifts (e.g., EU ETS auction cycles, regulatory changes) — forecasts remain flat or linear despite sharp changes.
- Forecasts are overly smooth — fail to capture sudden volatility or “jumps” in price, especially in the first 5–7 days of the horizon.
- Model tends to overfit recent low prices, producing a “floor” effect — forecasts stay near recent minima even when prices rebound.
- Model underestimates the impact of policy or market sentiment shifts — fails to anticipate sudden spikes or drops in the first 10 days.
